answer.text: 16 at metaphase I and 8 at metaphase II
answer.line: Copying once makes 16 chromatids at metaphase I. Meiosis I halves the chromosomes, but sisters stay joined: 8 at metaphase II.

steps: Count the copies first. 2n = 8 means 8 chromosomes, and S phase copies each one once, so metaphase I holds 16 chromatids.
Meiosis I pulls the homologs apart. Each new cell gets 4 chromosomes, and each is still two sister chromatids.
Sisters split only at anaphase II. So metaphase II holds 4 x 2 = 8 chromatids.

choices.text: 16 at metaphase I and 8 at metaphase II
choices.note: 8 chromosomes copied once make 16; half the chromosomes, still doubled, make 8.

choices.text: 16 at metaphase I and 16 at metaphase II
choices.note: This leaves out meiosis I. By metaphase II the cell has split once, so it holds half the DNA it had at metaphase I.

choices.text: 16 at metaphase I and 4 at metaphase II
